about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Troy Downing

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CROW TRIBE WATER RIGHTS SETTLEMENT AMENDMENTS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: CROW TRIBE WATER RIGHTS SETTLEMENT AMENDMENTS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Indian water rights settlements protect those rights by codifying them in Federal law and providing resources to promote water infrastructure development.
Without the ability to use settlement funds for water infrastructure, the Crow Reservation continues to face a clean water crisis.
Moreover, multiple further studies have linked the Tribe's higher cancer rates with this lack of clean water access.
In doing so, this legislation will dramatically reduce the timeline for delivering clean water to the reservation's communities.
S. 240 is a straightforward solution that does not alter any existing water rights and appropriates no new Federal spending.

Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act, as this legislation will make crucial adjustments to the Crow Tribe of Montana's water settlement, ensuring the Tribe can provide clean drinking water for its members for generations to come.
Senator Daines and I introduced the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act to directly address these challenges.
I urge my colleagues to vote in favor of this important legislation for the Crow Tribe.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REAUTHORIZING THE FORT PECK RESERVATION RURAL WATER SYSTEM ACT OF 2000
statements.title: REAUTHORIZING THE FORT PECK RESERVATION RURAL WATER SYSTEM ACT OF 2000

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SENATE MUST ACT
statements.title: SENATE MUST ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I will take this opportunity to recognize the importance of the passage of the 2026 farm bill.
I urge swift passage of the farm bill in the Senate. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NAHASDA NEEDS TO BE REAUTHORIZED
statements.title: NAHASDA NEEDS TO BE REAUTHORIZED
sentences: Thirty years ago, Congress passed a landmark Tribal housing law known as NAHASDA, which created the Indian Housing Block Grant program to promote self-determination.

I introduced the bipartisan and bicameral Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Modernization Act to eliminate red tape in Indian Country and further incentivize private financing.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this important legislation because it is Congress' responsibility to address the housing needs of all Americans. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LOWERING HOUSING COSTS AND ADVANCING MAIN STREET COMMUNITY BANKS
statements.title: LOWERING HOUSING COSTS AND ADVANCING MAIN STREET COMMUNITY BANKS
sentences: The National Association of Realtors estimates that the average first-time home buyer was 40 years old in the year 2025.

Looking forward, I believe we have the opportunity to make even more progress on housing by addressing reforms to the Build America Buy America Act, or BABA, and reauthorizing the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act, or NAHASDA.
NAHASDA is a lifeline for Indian Country, and its authorization lapsed after fiscal year 2013.
This law consolidated and authorized Indian housing programs, which provide Tribes greater autonomy when using Federal resources for housing projects on Tribal lands.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of H.R. 6644, the Housing for the 21st Century Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WISDOM FOR INNOVATIVE SMALL ENTERPRISES ACT
statements.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WISDOM FOR INNOVATIVE SMALL ENTERPRISES ACT
sentences: However, businesses with substantial and stable access to capital tend to be better positioned for technology adoption and dealing with its ramifications.

Small businesses, on the other hand, including businesses in rural communities like my home district in central and eastern Montana, often lack the resources and information needed to facilitate technology adoption.
While this figure may seem significant, it pales in comparison to the near-universal adoption of AI that is seen with Fortune 500 companies.
In doing so, this legislation seeks to provide small businesses with the technical and practical knowledge needed to best navigate AI adoption.

The scope of this educational material will include resources for small businesses on how AI models work, how businesses can identify tasks that AI can effectively perform, and the best practices for coordinating with third-party providers and protecting data privacy.
Madam Speaker, I rise in strong support of H.R. 5784, the AI-WISE Act.
Madam Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote in support of this legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHANGING HEALTH INSURANCE MARKET
statements.title: CHANGING HEALTH INSURANCE MARKET
sentences: Let's go back to the beginning of the unaffordable care act, ObamaCare.
The Affordable Care Act, ObamaCare, has been one of the biggest drivers in increasing not just the cost of health insurance but the cost of healthcare.
Now, let's look at the subsidies that have really gotten a lot of attention, these ObamaCare subsidies that we have been talking about that the Democrats brought in response to COVID.
These enhanced premium tax credits, or these ObamaCare credits, were designed to expire at the end of this year.
About 9 percent of that, was attributed to the enhanced premium tax credits, the ObamaCare credits.
Independent of these ObamaCare credits that we are discussing, it is going up in the small group, the large group, and it is going up in every other part of insurance.
One of the smallest increases we saw from our major payers was about 10, a little bit over 10 percent, and about 3 or 4 percent of that was attributed to the ObamaCare premiums.
They file, they are approved, they get filed with CMS, with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, and then the open enrollment period starts, which is usually mid-November to mid-December.
Mr. Speaker, during that open enrollment period is when you buy your policies for the following year.
We just closed that open enrollment period a couple of weeks ago for the 2026 policy years.

Unless we go to extraordinary measures of allowing the payers to, once again, refile their rates and then have another open enrollment period, which I guess would be March or April by the time we got all that through, then, what do we with that?
The point I am making is that by extending those ObamaCare subsidies, we are not affecting the 2026 rates without going to extraordinary measures to unroll everything that has already happened.

What will happen is those insurance companies that filed higher rates with the assumption of those premium tax credits staying in will get the benefit of having a higher rate plus having that tax credit.
This ObamaCare premium debacle is not the answer, but we do need to get to work and figure out how we can get to the root causes of these rising prices.
I will tell you, all of that--I will tell you; this is one time that both the Republicans and Democrats agree, that it did not deliver on that.

That is because, as I said, this is either going to collapse under its own weight or we are going to be forced to write an unlimited check to the Federal Government which many of my colleagues and I are unwilling to do.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SBA FRAUD ENFORCEMENT EXTENSION ACT
statements.title: SBA FRAUD ENFORCEMENT EXTENSION ACT
sentences: If Congress does not act, law enforcement will not have the necessary time to investigate and prosecute these crimes.
This extension will provide critical time for law enforcement to track down criminals who have defrauded the U.S. Government and hold them accountable.
Small businesses across our country, including in my home district of central and eastern Montana, deserve an SBA that efficiently supports local job creators and isn't undercut by fraud.

It is essential that law enforcement is given the proper tools, time, and authority to punish those who subvert the integrity of the SBA programs and ensure that fraudsters face consequences for their actions.
Along with my colleague, Representative Conaway, I have introduced H.R. 4495, the SBA Fraud Enforcement Extension Act.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "MILES CITY FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "MILES CITY FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN...

It is about putting working families before bureaucrats.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of my resolution, H.J. Res. 104.
I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' on H.J. Res. 104 and send a clear message that energy security, economic stability, and the voices of rural America will not be ignored.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CAPITAL FOR RURAL JOB CREATORS ACT
statements.title: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CAPITAL FOR RURAL JOB CREATORS ACT
sentences: These overlooked people and places have inspired my legislation, H.R. 1190, the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAFEGUARDING PROPERTY
statements.title: SAFEGUARDING PROPERTY
sentences: In the 119th Congress, House Republicans have sent a clear message to criminal illegal aliens: If you break our laws, you go home.
Earlier this year, we passed the Laken Riley Act.
My Safeguarding American Property Act builds on the good work of the Laken Riley Act by expanding the bill to include property crimes like trespassing and arson as deportable offenses.

Mitigating these types of property crimes is a particularly important challenge for border States and rural districts like mine which often have vast distances between homes and businesses and in which law enforcement resources are often spread thin.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all of my colleagues to support the Safeguarding American Property Act to further strengthen the good policies codified in the Laken Riley Act. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WORK HIGHLIGHTS OF WESTERN CAUCUS
statements.title: WORK HIGHLIGHTS OF WESTERN CAUCUS
sentences: This last one recognizes the rich natural resources we have in the great State of Montana right underneath our feet.

Our bill encourages domestic production, decreases reliance on foreign minerals, shores up supply chains, and significantly bolsters national security, all while dealing a critical blow to Putin's war machine.
We introduced the Stop Russian Market Manipulation Act.
With bicameral support, I am confident we will get this bill across the finish line for our Tribal communities and our State economy.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING THE RIGHTS AND SAFETY OF WOMEN
statements.title: PROTECTING THE RIGHTS AND SAFETY OF WOMEN
sentences: Last week, we considered bills to hold accountable illegal aliens who break our laws and defend U.S. national sovereignty against a rogue international judicial body.
Just yesterday, we passed H.R. 28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
I was proud to add my support to this critical legislation, and I look forward to voting for a second bill, the Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act, on the House floor tomorrow.
H.R. 30 will ensure that illegal aliens who have been convicted of or admit to committing sex offenses or domestic violence can be deported by closing a loophole in existing law.
